what: Two published sources behind the reading that the CAMELS rain table (Daymet) stamps rain by a day that ends in the morning. They were looked up on 2026-10-03 by the project lead (the Claude Code session) through a web fetch of the pages below; no team member has read them yet.

sources.reference: Thornton, P. E., Shrestha, R., Thornton, M., Kao, S.-C., Wei, Y., Wilson, B. E. (2021). Gridded daily weather data for North America with comprehensive uncertainty quantification. Scientific Data, 8, 190.
what_it_says: It is the paper of Daymet version 4.
Daily precipitation observations that are taken once a day but not from midnight to midnight local standard time can put all or part of a rain event on the wrong calendar day.
In version 4 the recorded precipitation of stations with a time of observation before noon local standard time is shifted back one day.
This timing bias was not examined in earlier versions of Daymet.
sources.wording: paraphrased from the retrieved page, not copied word for word
sources.what_it_does_not_say: It does not mention CAMELS. That CAMELS holds an earlier version follows from the dates only: CAMELS was published in 2015, Daymet version 4 in 2021.

sources.reference: Kratzert, F., Klotz, D., Hochreiter, S., Nearing, G. S. (2021). A note on leveraging synergy in multiple meteorological data sets with deep learning for rainfall-runoff modeling. Hydrology and Earth System Sciences, 25, 2685-2703.
what_it_says: A lag-correlation analysis of the precipitation products in CAMELS found a higher correlation between Daymet and Maurer when Maurer was lagged by one day in 325 of 531 basins.
Gridded products differ in how they define a calendar day.
sources.wording: paraphrased from the retrieved page, not copied word for word
sources.what_it_does_not_say: It does not say at what hour the Daymet day ends.

how_to_word_it: The day stamp is an inference from our own correlations (results/rain_timing.json; measured against hourly rain in results/day_windows.json if that file exists). It is consistent with a time-of-observation effect that the Daymet authors describe and correct from version 4 on, and with the one-day shifts between CAMELS rain products reported by Kratzert et al. The documentation of the Daymet version inside CAMELS was not checked.
notes: The team should read both passages themselves before the review (RS/GIS member 2 owns the satellite and rain-data part).
